Stack used and available points for a habitat-selection model

Source: R/used_available.R
used_available.Rd

Stacks the used points of sample_locations() and the available points of sample_available() into the long table a conditional logistic regression takes: one stratum per animal, bin and draw, holding its one used point (case = 1) and its available points (case = 0), with one column per layer of layers read at each point's cell. This is the use-availability design, which compares the resources an animal used with those available to it (Johnson 1980).

Usage

used_available(presence, available, layers)

Arguments

presence

The used points: a data frame with animal_id, bin_start (POSIXct, UTC), draw, x and y, one row per animal, bin and draw, such as the output of sample_locations().

available

The available points from sample_available() for the same presence.

layers

A SpatRaster of covariates on the grid of the points, one layer per covariate, each with a name that becomes a column.

Value

A data frame with one row per point: stratum (an integer per animal, bin and draw), case (1 used, 0 available), animal_id, bin_start, draw, cell, x, y, and one column per layer, ordered by stratum with the used point first. Attributes: "estimand" and "n"

from available, "epsg", and "dropped", a data frame of rows dropped by case and reason.

Details

Each point is read at the cell of layers that holds its x and y. A cell column in presence or available must name that same cell, or the points were drawn on another grid and the call stops.

A row with a missing layer value is dropped, and the attribute dropped counts the rows by reason. A stratum whose used point has a missing value is dropped whole, as is a stratum left with no available point; a used point whose stratum has no available points in available (a stratum that sample_available() dropped) is dropped too. Every kept stratum therefore holds one used point and at least one available point, and without missing values exactly attr(available, "n") of them. A warning gives the counts whenever a row is dropped.

The function fits no model. A conditional logit per animal on one draw's strata, such as survival::clogit(case ~ depth_m + strata(stratum), data = d[d$draw == 1, ]), gives one imputation; repeating it for each draw and pooling with Rubin's rules carries the position uncertainty of the surfaces. Fitting every draw at once treats one position as many and narrows the interval. Columns of presence other than the ones named below are not carried.

References

Johnson, D. H. (1980). The comparison of usage and availability measurements for evaluating resource preference. Ecology, 61, 65-71. doi:10.2307/1937156

See also

sample_locations(), sample_available()

Examples

tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers, max_distance = 2000)
model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,
                         stoney_track$tags)
presence <- sample_locations(location_surface(counts, field), n = 5, seed = 1)
listening <- expand.grid(station_id = stoney_track$receivers$station_id,
                         date = unique(as.Date(presence$bin_start, tz = "UTC")),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
hourly <- system_de(field, listening, transmissions = 24)
available <- sample_available(presence, hourly, grid, n = 20, seed = 1)
# Bottom depth in metres, positive down, as the covariate
depth <- abs(grid)
names(depth) <- "depth_m"
stacked <- used_available(presence, available, depth)
head(stacked)
#>   stratum case animal_id           bin_start draw  cell      x       y
#> 1       1    1 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  2502 735254 4940491
#> 2       1    0 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  4826 732454 4939091
#> 3       1    0 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  6432 725054 4938091
#> 4       1    0 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  8293 726354 4936991
#> 5       1    0 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1 17329 722754 4931591
#> 6       1    0 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1  3831 733754 4939691
#>      depth_m
#> 1  0.4259501
#> 2 12.0942841
#> 3  0.9803903
#> 4  7.2122607
#> 5  7.6489463
#> 6  9.0104446
table(case = stacked$case)
#> case
#>     0     1 
#> 21200  1060
